metaDescription: Bobrick B262 towel dispenser review for commercial restrooms: 400 C-fold / 525 multifold capacity, 22-gauge 304 stainless durability, and quote comparison.
excerpt: The Bobrick B-262 ClassicSeries is the most widely specified surface-mounted 304 stainless steel paper towel dispenser in US commercial office buildings. Our technical review breaks down its 4-inch ADA projection, 400 C-fold / 525 multifold sheet capacity, hemmed towel opening, and lifecycle economics versus roll dispensers.
quickAnswer: In our commercial facility assessment, the Bobrick B-262 ClassicSeries earns its industry-standard status through all-welded 22-gauge Type 304 satin stainless steel construction, a true 4-inch wall depth that passes ADA 307 corridor protrusion inspections without recessing, and a hemmed opening that holds 400 C-fold or 525 multifold towels without tearing wet paper. While offices with 75+ employees per restroom core benefit from upgrading to 1,150-foot hard roll systems like Scott Pro to lower night janitorial restocking labor ($35 to $65/hr), the B-262 remains the gold standard for single-occupant ADA restrooms, office kitchenettes, and 2,500 to 15,000 sq ft professional suites.

blocks.text: Why the Bobrick B-262 Is the Benchmark in US Commercial Construction

Walk into almost any Class A or Class B commercial office building, medical clinic, or corporate breakroom across the United States, and you will likely encounter the Bobrick B-262 ClassicSeries mounted next to the sink. Architects specify the B-262 on CSI Division 10 (10 28 00 Toilet, Bath, and Laundry Accessories) blueprints by default because it solves two recurring headaches for general contractors and property managers: it installs directly onto finished drywall or tile without cutting into fire-rated wall studs, and its exactly 4-inch depth meets federal ADA protrusion codes.

In this bobrick b262 towel dispenser review, we examine the unit from the perspective of an ongoing facility operations budget—looking at its 22-gauge Type 304 metallurgy, how night janitorial crews interact with its universal Bobrick B-262-60 key lock during $15 to $30 per-visit restroom services, and how its consumable throughput compares against high-capacity 1.75-inch core hard roll towel systems.
Detailed Technical Specs & Build Quality Assessment
Unlike generic stamped-metal cabinets that rattle when pulled or rust along spot-welded corners, the Bobrick B-262 is built to commercial institutional standards:

items: Dimensions & True 4-Inch ADA Profile: Measuring 10-3/4 inches wide by 14 inches high by exactly 4 inches deep (275 x 355 x 100 mm), the B-262 satisfies 2010 ADA Standards Section 307.2 for protruding objects even when surface-mounted on an open circulation path between 27 and 80 inches above the finished floor.

22-Gauge Type 304 Satin Stainless Steel Construction: Both the cabinet chassis and door are formed from 22-gauge (0.8 mm) Type 304 (18-8) stainless steel with a No. 4 directional satin finish on all exposed surfaces. The door swings down on a full-length heavy-duty stainless piano hinge secured at the bottom, preventing sagging over years of daily janitorial openings.

Hemmed Towel Tray Opening: The bottom towel dispensing slot features a fully rolled-under hemmed edge. Even when an employee pulls a damp 1-ply recycled multifold towel downward at a sharp angle, the hemmed steel guides the sheet cleanly without slicing the paper fiber or scraping knuckles.

Dual-Format Paper Capacity & Side Sight Slots: The internal hopper accepts 400 C-fold towels or 525 multifold towels measuring 3-1/8 to 3-13/16 inches deep without requiring any plastic adapter insert. Narrow vertical refill-indicator slots punched into the lower sides let custodians verify paper depth at a glance.

blocks.title: ADA Mounting Height Rule for the Bobrick B-262
blocks.text: When installing a surface-mounted Bobrick B-262 over an unobstructed floor area, mount the unit so the bottom towel dispensing slot sits at 40 to 48 inches maximum above the finished floor. If mounting over a lavatory countertop or breakroom base cabinet that is 20 to 25 inches deep, ADA Section 308.2.2 reduces the maximum unobstructed forward reach height to 44 inches maximum AFF to the towel slot.
Bobrick B-262 vs. High-Capacity Roll Towel & Office Consumables Matrix

For an office suite under 10,000 sq ft (where baseline janitorial rates run $0.09 to $0.15 per sq ft for 2,500–9,999 sq ft, or $0.12 to $0.20 per sq ft under 2,500 sq ft), the B-262's 525-sheet multifold capacity easily handles daily handwashing. However, in larger multi-tenant floor plates (10,000 to 24,999 sq ft at $0.07 to $0.12 per sq ft), facility directors frequently pair B-262 units in breakrooms with high-footage roll towels, jumbo bath tissue, facial tissue cubes, and commercial liners across the rest of the suite. blocks.text: Solving the Two Classic Bobrick B-262 Operational Pain Points
While the B-262 hardware itself is practically indestructible, facility managers who inherit a building outfitted with B-262 units should correct two frequent operational friction points:

items.name: Stop Buying C-Fold Towels—Stock Interfolded Multifold Only
items.text: The B-262 is rated for 400 C-fold or 525 multifold towels. Because C-fold sheets do not interleave, users reach up into the hemmed slot and pull out clumps of 3 to 5 wet sheets, driving up your annual paper budget and overflowing trash receptacles. Switching strictly to standard 9.125 x 9.5 inch multifold packs increases cabinet capacity by 31% (525 vs. 400 sheets) and forces single-sheet dispensing.

items.name: Prevent Door Flap Drop by Keeping Spare Bobrick Cat-74 Keys on Carts
items.text: When night janitors lose the standard Bobrick tumbler key, they sometimes force the top latch open with a flathead screwdriver, bending the lock cam so the stainless door drops open onto the sink when pulled. Clip two spare Bobrick universal keys onto every night janitor cart keyring and inspect the top lock pawl during quarterly facility walkthroughs.

items.name: Deploy Facial Tissue Cubes in Conference Rooms to Curb Towel Pilferage
items.text: In offices lacking desktop tissue, employees routinely pull a stack of 15 multifold towels from the kitchenette or restroom B-262 to keep at their workstation. Placing Kleenex Professional Facial Tissue Cube Boxes (36-case, 95 2-ply FSC-certified sheets per box) across conference rooms, reception desks, and shared islands protects your restroom towel inventory.

items.name: Pair B-262 Restrooms with High-Endurance Roll Tissue & Two-Tier Liners
items.text: Keep night janitorial restocking efficient by supplying Scott Essential Jumbo Roll Toilet Paper 2-Ply (12 x 1,000-foot rolls, 3.25-inch core) in the stalls, Boardwalk 24x33 8-micron high-density liners (1,000-case) for workstation bins, and Genuine Joe 33x39 1.5-mil heavy-duty 33-gallon liners (100-case) for the main wet towel receptacle beneath your B-262.

blocks.title: Adding the Bobrick Skirt or Paper-Saver Insert for Narrow Folded Towels
blocks.text: If your office switches to compact eco-sized multifold towels (under 3-1/8 inches folded depth) that occasionally slip through the standard B-262 opening, Bobrick manufactures the TowelMate accessory module that installs inside any existing B-262 cabinet in two minutes—adding a center rod that separates sheets and reduces folded towel usage by another 15% to 20%.

faqs.q: What size paper towels fit the Bobrick B-262 dispenser?
faqs.a: The Bobrick B-262 accepts standard commercial C-fold towels (up to 400 sheets) and standard multifold towels (up to 525 sheets) with a folded width of 9 to 9.5 inches and a folded depth between 3-1/8 and 3-13/16 inches. Always verify that your janitorial crew does not pack towels above the top of the side sight slots, as overpacking compresses the stack and causes tearing.

faqs.q: When should an office choose a hard roll towel system over the Bobrick B-262?
faqs.a: The B-262 is ideal for breakrooms, kitchenettes ($12 to $25 per visit sanitation add-on), and restrooms serving 10 to 45 people daily where a 4-inch ADA wall profile and zero battery maintenance are priorities. Once a central restroom serves 60+ employees daily on a 5x-week night cleaning schedule (21.65 visits/month), switching to a 1,150-foot hard roll system like Scott Pro (6,900 linear feet per 6-roll case) prevents late-afternoon towel runouts.

faqs.q: Does the Bobrick B-262 meet 2010 ADA Standards without recessing into the wall?
faqs.a: Yes. Under 2010 ADA Standards Section 307.2, objects mounted on walls with their leading edges between 27 inches and 80 inches above the finished floor may protrude a maximum of 4.0 inches into circulation paths. Because the B-262 has an exact 4.0-inch depth, it achieves full ADA compliance when surface-mounted directly onto tile or drywall.

faqs.q: How do facility managers prevent white streaks or corrosion on a B-262 satin finish?
faqs.a: Specify in your janitorial contract that cleaners must never spray bleach, acid bowl cleaners, or unbuffered high-alkaline degreasers onto the Type 304 stainless steel housing. A damp microfiber cloth with neutral-pH cleaner wiped strictly parallel to the horizontal satin grain removes water spots and preserves the factory corrosion barrier indefinitely.
